# Research Note: Exxon Mobil Corporation (XOM)
**Date:** May 3, 2026

---

## Snapshot

**Company:** Exxon Mobil Corporation (XOM) – Oil & Gas Integrated  
**Current Price:** $152.75 USD [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]  
**Market Capitalization:** $634.9 billion [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]  
**P/E Ratio:** 25.72 (trailing), 18.07 (FMP adjusted) [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance; Financial Modeling Prep]  
**52-Week Range:** $101.19 - $176.41 [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]  
**1-Month Price Change:** -4.94% [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]

**Recent Performance:**  
XOM shares declined 4.94% over the past month, reflecting profit-taking after Q1 2026 earnings that beat estimates but showed year-over-year declines due to Middle East disruptions and refining margin compression [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]. The stock trades 13.4% below its 52-week high of $176.41 [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance].

**Macro Context:**  
The Federal Funds Rate stands at 3.64% (falling trend), while unemployment has risen to 4.3% and inflation continues to rise (CPI at 330.29) [Source: FRED Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis]. The 10Y-2Y Treasury spread is positive at 0.51 bps but falling, suggesting a normalizing but uncertain rate environment [Source: FRED Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis]. The S&P 500 is at 7,230.12 (rising trend), indicating broader market strength despite energy sector volatility [Source: FRED Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis].

---

## Bull Case

**1. Record Production Growth in Strategic Assets**  
Excluding external disruptions, Upstream production rose 8% year-over-year in Q1 2026, driven by the Permian Basin and Guyana [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. Management confirmed the company remains on track to reach 1.8 million oil-equivalent barrels per day in full-year 2026 Permian output, with long-term targets of approximately 2 million barrels per day [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. Guyana achieved record production with high reliability, and three major projects (Oahu, Whiptail, Hammerhead) are under construction, with Oahu expected to deliver first oil by year-end [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/].

**2. Pioneer Acquisition Synergies Driving Permian Dominance**  
The October 2023 acquisition of Pioneer Natural Resources, completed in May 2024, more than doubled Permian production to 1.3 million barrels per day and created an estimated 16 billion barrels of oil equivalent resource base [Source: https://corporate.exxonmobil.com/news/news-releases/2024/0503_exxonmobil-completes-acquisition-of-pioneer-natural-resources]. The combined 1.4 million net acres of highly contiguous acreage enables deployment of proprietary technology and capital efficiency improvements that neither company could achieve standalone [Source: https://corporate.exxonmobil.com/news/news-releases/2024/0503_exxonmobil-completes-acquisition-of-pioneer-natural-resources].

**3. Downstream Excellence Offsetting Upstream Volatility**  
The Energy Products segment delivered $2.8 billion in Q1 2026 earnings, up $2 billion year-over-year and several hundred million sequentially from Q4 2025 [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. Gulf Coast refineries operated at record utilization rates, and March throughput increased by 200,000 barrels per day versus February as maintenance was expedited [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. The 2023 Beaumont refinery expansion has fully recovered its investment ahead of expectations [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/].

**4. LNG Capacity Expansion at Critical Juncture**  
Golden Pass LNG achieved first LNG in March 2026, with Train 1 increasing U.S. LNG exports by approximately 5% relative to 2025; all three trains are expected to boost total U.S. exports by about 15% [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. Mozambique and Papua New Guinea LNG projects are expected to reach final investment decisions later in 2026, adding portfolio diversification and capacity [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/].

**5. Disciplined Capital Returns Despite Earnings Pressure**  
XOM maintains a quarterly dividend of $1.03 per share ($4.12 annualized, 2.58% yield), representing 44 consecutive years of dividend increases [Source: https://www.koyfin.com/company/xom/dividends/]. The company has completed a $71.65 billion buyback program since 2021, retiring over 16% of shares, with $20 billion per year in ongoing buybacks [Source: https://www.sahmcapital.com/news/content/exxons-dividend-growth-and-major-buybacks-might-change-the-case-for-investing-in-exxon-mobil-xom-2026-02-13]. This combination supports per-share metrics even during earnings cyclicality [Source: https://www.sahmcapital.com/news/content/exxons-dividend-growth-and-major-buybacks-might-change-the-case-for-investing-in-exxon-mobil-xom-2026-02-13].

---

## Bear Case

**1. Year-Over-Year Earnings Decline Despite Oil Price Surge**  
Q1 2026 earnings of $1.16 per share (adjusted) represented a significant decline from $2.09 per share in Q1 2025, despite oil prices rising during the quarter [Source: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/05/02/while-oil-prices-skyrocketed-in-the-first-quarter/]. Reported GAAP earnings were only $1.00 per share ($4.2 billion), down from higher prior-year levels [Source: https://investor.exxonmobil.com/company-information/press-releases/detail/1204/exxonmobil-announces-first-quarter-2026-results]. The disconnect between rising crude prices and falling profitability raises concerns about operational efficiency and margin compression [Source: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/05/02/while-oil-prices-skyrocketed-in-the-first-quarter/].

**2. Material Middle East Infrastructure Damage with Multi-Year Recovery**  
Drone attacks damaged two LNG trains in Qatar representing approximately 3% of global production, with CEO Darren Woods stating "repair time will be anywhere between three and five years" [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. External events including the Middle East conflict, drone attacks in Kazakhstan, and a Permian winter storm adversely affected Q1 upstream production [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. Management noted the market "has not seen the full impact" of Middle East disruptions [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/].

**3. Refining and Chemical Margin Compression**  
Global refining crack spreads were compressed in Q1 2026 by weak gasoline demand in the Northern Hemisphere winter and elevated crude feedstock costs from the late-quarter oil price surge [Source: https://news.alphastreet.com/exxon-mobil-xom-2026-earnings-preview-record-production-meets-flat-oil-prices-ahead-of-may-1-report/]. The Chemical Products segment continues to face global oversupply in commodity chemicals including ethylene and polyethylene, limiting earnings recovery [Source: https://news.alphastreet.com/exxon-mobil-xom-2026-earnings-preview-record-production-meets-flat-oil-prices-ahead-of-may-1-report/].

**4. Limited Production Response to Political Pressure**  
Despite President Trump's calls for increased output due to Middle East energy concerns, XOM's CFO confirmed there would be no alterations in Permian Basin production strategies, prioritizing free cash flow over volume growth [Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8838259/exxon-mobil-xom-and-chevron-cvx-maintain-production-strategies-amid-market-pressures]. This disciplined approach may limit revenue upside in a tight supply environment but reflects management's focus on returns over growth [Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8838259/exxon-mobil-xom-and-chevron-cvx-maintain-production-strategies-amid-market-pressures].

**5. High Valuation Relative to Historical Norms**  
At a trailing P/E of 25.72, XOM trades at a premium to its historical average and significantly above the adjusted P/E of 18.07, suggesting limited multiple expansion potential [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance; Financial Modeling Prep]. The stock's 13.4% decline from 52-week highs indicates market skepticism about near-term earnings trajectory [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance].

---

## Recent Catalysts

**Q1 2026 Earnings Beat (May 1-2, 2026)**  
XOM reported Q1 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.16 versus $0.98 consensus (17.9% beat) and revenue of $85.1 billion versus $81.1 billion estimate (4.9% beat) [Source: https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/XOM/q1-2026/]. Shares declined 1.0% following the release as results were largely in line with expectations despite the headline beat [Source: https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/XOM/q1-2026/]. 
[Filing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408826000065/xom-20260501.htm]

**Golden Pass LNG First Production (March 2026)**  
The Golden Pass LNG facility achieved first LNG in March 2026, representing a major milestone in U.S. LNG export capacity expansion [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. Train 1 alone increases U.S. LNG exports by ~5%, with total facility capacity expected to boost exports by ~15% when all three trains are operational [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/].

**Middle East Conflict Impact (Ongoing Q1 2026)**  
Conflict-related disruptions affected operations and resulted in material infrastructure damage to Qatar LNG facilities, with two trains offline for 3-5 years [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. CEO Woods emphasized the company's global scale enabled effective supply chain management and customer delivery despite disruptions [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/].

**Low Carbon Solutions Expansion (Q1 2026)**  
XOM began transporting and storing CO2 from the New Generation Gas Gathering Project, the second such startup within a year, with plans for additional 4 million tons per year capture capacity within the next two years [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/].

**Annual Report Filing (February 18, 2026)**  
The 10-K for fiscal year 2025 was filed, providing comprehensive disclosure on operations, risks, and strategic priorities. 
[Filing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408826000045/xom-20251231.htm]

## Risks

**Geopolitical Exposure**  
The Middle East conflict has already resulted in material production losses (approximately 3% of global LNG capacity offline for 3-5 years) and ongoing operational disruptions [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. Additional geopolitical risks include Kazakhstan operations (subject to drone attacks), Venezuela opportunities (dependent on investment climate), and Guyana (regulatory and operational complexity) [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/].

**Commodity Price Volatility**  
Despite rising oil prices in Q1 2026, earnings declined year-over-year, highlighting the company's exposure to downstream margins, chemical spreads, and inventory timing effects that can offset crude price strength [Source: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/05/02/while-oil-prices-skyrocketed-in-the-first-quarter/]. Management noted unfavorable timing effects of $3.9 billion ($0.93 per share) in Q1 that will unwind in subsequent periods [Source: https://investor.exxonmobil.com/company-information/press-releases/detail/1204/exxonmobil-announces-first-quarter-2026-results].

**Macro Headwinds**  
Rising unemployment (4.3%) and persistent inflation (CPI 330.29, rising trend) could dampen demand for refined products and chemicals [Source: FRED Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis]. Falling Federal Funds Rate (3.64%, falling trend) suggests potential economic softness that may pressure energy demand [Source: FRED Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis].

**Transition and Regulatory Risk**  
While XOM is investing in low-carbon solutions (carbon capture, hydrogen, low-emission fuels), the pace and economics of energy transition remain uncertain [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]. Regulatory changes affecting oil and gas production, emissions standards, or carbon pricing could materially impact economics [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance].

**Chemical Segment Structural Oversupply**  
Global oversupply in commodity chemicals (ethylene, polyethylene) is a structural challenge that may persist, limiting earnings recovery in this segment independent of oil price movements [Source: https://news.alphastreet.com/exxon-mobil-xom-2026-earnings-preview-record-production-meets-flat-oil-prices-ahead-of-may-1-report/].

---

## What to Watch Next

**1. Q2 2026 Earnings (Next Report: August 7, 2026)**  
The next earnings report will be critical to assess whether Q1's timing effects unwind as management projected (adding $0.93 per share) and whether Middle East operations stabilize [Source: Financial Modeling Prep; https://investor.exxonmobil.com/company-information/press-releases/detail/1204/exxonmobil-announces-first-quarter-2026-results]. Monitor refining margins, chemical spreads, and whether Permian production maintains its trajectory toward 1.8 million barrels per day [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/].

**2. LNG Project Sanction Decisions (H2 2026)**  
Final investment decisions on Mozambique and Papua New Guinea LNG projects are expected later in 2026, which would significantly expand XOM's LNG portfolio and diversify geographic exposure [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. Guyana's Oahu project first oil (expected year-end 2026) will also be a key operational milestone [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/].

**3. Middle East Recovery Timeline and Insurance Settlement**  
The three-to-five-year repair timeline for Qatar LNG trains represents a material earnings headwind [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. Clarity on insurance recovery timing and amounts, as well as progress on infrastructure repairs, will be important for modeling long-term cash flows [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/]. Management indicated direct loss coverage is not expected to be a significant constraint, but details remain pending [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/01/exxonmobil-xom-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/].
